instruction_summary: Study B (002-theory-update): write the 'Theory, updated to 2026' section of the IKKS (2007) welfare-reform paper as a model, using Study A's 2009-2026 EUROMOD rates - inverse-optimum reading (Saez 2002), elasticity frontier by era with literature overlay, one minimal amendment + one rejected alternative, a linearisation consistency check, and a Belgium cost-per-job external validation. CPU only, no EUROMOD, no fetches.

steps.description: Rebuilt CPU venv (numpy/pandas/scipy/xlrd/matplotlib); linked EUROMOD.xls and shared-data; copied welfare_core.py, fixed_inputs.py; imported welfare_layer.py from 002-living-update-cont (read-only)
steps.command: uv venv /workspace/.venv && uv pip install numpy pandas scipy xlrd matplotlib

steps.description: Item 1: inverse-optimum g_d (Saez 2002) for 1998 + 2009-2026, all 14 V countries; DK 1998 reproduction + agreement table vs 001 Pareto flags [CONSISTENCY CHECK]
Item 2: elasticity frontier by era in (eta_avg,eps) space; per-country survival vs literature elasticities
Item 3: minimal amendment - reallocate eta onto secondary earners/lone parents (groups 2,7-10), aggregate held fixed; recompute ranking
Item 4: linearisation accuracy check [CONSISTENCY CHECK] - fit d_PTR->d_Psi_w on 2009-2017, predict 2018-2026
Item 4b: Belgium external validation - model cost per participant/FTE of a marginal lump-sum in-work transfer vs de Mahieu (2021)
Item 5: calibration table (1998 vs 2026 parameters/moments with sources)
Deliverable figures (frontier by era + supporting critical-eta/g figure), PNG+PDF

key_results.DK_1998_inverse_optimum_reproduced: decile-1 g = -0.73 < 0 in a working-poor-gainer decile; D_w=-1.654 matches table2a.csv
key_results.amendment_secondary_earners_2026_ranking: 8->7 of 10 stable (one flip: IT); composition not the driver
key_results.rejected_alternative: Kroft et al. 2020 unemployment/wage channel [PROPOSED] - not calibrable from 001 artefacts
key_results.BE_verdict: model below published range (self-financing at benchmark eta) - pre-declared expected direction

comparison_to_original.note: g-iff flags only DK in 1998, matching the paper's strict statement

comparison_to_original.followup: 2026: 0/14 at US-EITC eta~0, 5/14 at EU eta~0.11, 9/14 at Chetty 0.25
comparison_to_original.note: survives mid-range, strengthened post-2017, collapses at US-EITC floor

comparison_to_original.quantity: Critical avg elasticity for Psi_w<Psi_d (panel, eps=0.1)
comparison_to_original.original: n/a (paper gives Table-3 criticals only at 1998)
comparison_to_original.note: in-work dominance now holds at lower elasticities

comparison_to_original.quantity: Cost per FTE of marginal in-work transfer, Belgium
comparison_to_original.note: below range, pre-declared direction: lump-sum no phase-out; self-financing at high BE bottom-decile PTRs

deviations: No new EUROMOD rates by design (spec §11): reuses Study A's rates and code; inherits all its limitations (V4/q=0 headline, Psi-instability at the bottom, gross-basis EL/IT, IE-2021 gap, UK out of scope, 1998->2009 method break).
Strict g<0 'iff' over-predicts Pareto in 2026 for AT/NL/ES (participation-trap, Psi-unstable); reported as a consistency-check artifact, not a finding.
Frontier across-era panel is the 5 countries stable in all four eras {FI,FR,EL,IT,SE}; per-country values for all 14 in frontier_survival.csv.
Linearisation check uses small n (6 fit/7 test) because Psi_w is finite+stable for few country-years; the negative out-of-sample R2 is itself the point.
Bartels-Shupe eta operationalised as flat 0.11 (mid of 0.08 men/0.14 women) in the frontier survival counts and the BE check; split noted.
External validation covers Belgium only (the sole study country with a cited behavioural cost-per-job estimate).
